finding.title: Guard ref.mounted after await in SacredLocationNotifier/InIsraelNotifier mutator methods
finding.why: detect() awaits a GPS fix with a 15-second timeout then unconditionally writes state/invalidates ref on success; setManualCity, setManualCoords and InIsraelNotifier.setInIsrael likewise touch state/ref after an await with no ref.mounted check. This file's own _load() methods DO guard (comment: 'an account switch rebuilds it. Never write state on a disposed notifier'), and the paired test file carries a regression test titled 'was a race' proving the team already hit a real race in this exact provider once. If the notifier is disposed while one of these four unguarded methods is mid-await (profile/account switch during a slow GPS fetch is the obvious trigger), Riverpod 3 throws UnmountedRefException, which nothing in the call chain catches (the caller's try/finally in sacred_time_settings_card.dart has no catch clause).
finding.recommendation: Add `if (!ref.mounted) return;` immediately after every await in detect(), setManualCity(), setManualCoords(), setInIsrael(), and _pushSnapshot() before the next ref/state touch, mirroring the guard already used in _load().
acceptance_criteria: Every async Notifier method in sacred_location_provider.dart checks ref.mounted after each await before touching ref/state
A new test disposes/invalidates the ProviderContainer while detect()/setManualCity() is mid-await (e.g. a Completer-backed fake LocationService) and asserts no UnmountedRefException propagates
